title: Normalized continuous finite-field coefficient presentations
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime and $X$ any scheme. Equip the native abelian coefficient ring $B_X$ of [def-sf-locally-finite-adic-realization-data] with its existing commutative monoid structure. For every finite coefficient field $E$ in the algebraic closure of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, with the size transport and specified embedding of [def-sf-locally-finite-adic-realization-data], there is a CoefficientPresentation: its integral comparison identifies continuous integral functions with the completed constant residue tower, its finite comparisons fix constants and recover pointwise residues, and its integral localization and inclusions have their specified pointwise normalizations. These presentations can be chosen simultaneously so that for $E\le L$ the completed coefficient map followed by the $L$ integral map into $B_X$ equals the $E$ integral map.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficient-completion] to every finite field. The finite quotient comparisons fix constants. Compare the two limiting residue cones to obtain the integral isomorphism, retaining its equations after every positive projection.

Use [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficient-localization] for the normalized localization isomorphism and the integral-to-rational map of [def-sfb-continuous-coefficient-pullback-maps]. Postcomposition by the specified field embedding lands in locally finite functions because the field is finite dimensional. Pointwise ring operations and precomposition give the native sheaf morphism and its normalization.

For an extension of finite fields, compare integral sections after every residue projection. For each target residue precision, continuity supplies a sufficiently deep source precision whose ideal maps into the target ideal. The defining completion map applies the field inclusion at these precisions; compatibility on deepening the source precision covers ramification. Joint injectivity of the inverse-limit projections identifies the integral section; then the two composite embeddings in the algebraic closure agree. This gives the scalar equation. Empty objects and identity extensions obey the same formulas.

theorem coefficientPresentations_exists
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsCommMonObj (abRing l X)] :
    ∃ coefficient : ∀ E : Index l (PadicAlgCl l),
      CoefficientPresentation l X (Coefficient.{u} l (PadicAlgCl l) E) (embedding l E),
      ∀ (E L : Index l (PadicAlgCl l)) (h : E ≤ L),
        completedCoefficientMap l (Coefficient.{u} l (PadicAlgCl l) E)
            (Coefficient.{u} l (PadicAlgCl l) L)
            (coefficientInclusion l (PadicAlgCl l) E L h) X ≫
          (coefficient L).integralMap l X = (coefficient E).integralMap l X
